corridor.title: Green Corridor

intro.heading: Green Corridor cost model
intro.body: Evaluate a green shipping corridor: the NPV cost gap between running it on green fuel versus fossil fuel, with EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime, IRA 45Z and custom regulation layered on top. Fill in the five steps — each covers one area of the model — and read the results in the always-visible panel. Benchmarks fill every field; override only what you know better.

cargo.waccHelp: Benchmarked by country — override with a project-specific cost of capital. The country table is illustrative, not a verified source.
cargo.countryHelp: The corridor's anchor country — port A's country — selects the financing (WACC) benchmark. Denmark, Netherlands, India, Brazil, Singapore and the United States carry workbook benchmarks; every other country uses the generic benchmark. Ports and the second country are descriptive.
cargo.unitWeightHelp: What one cargo unit weighs. Used to derive cost per tonne of cargo; the model itself counts units.
cargo.portCoordsHelp: Functional for build-here: the plant→port logistics leg computes from these coordinates. Leave untouched otherwise.

vessel.capexGreenHelp: Whole-fleet figure — the vessel count multiplies fuel and regulation only, never this cell. Benchmark = vessel type × (1 + green-fuel readiness premium), single hull.
vessel.capexFossilHelp: Whole-fleet figure. Benchmark 0 — existing baseline fleet; override when the comparison builds new fossil tonnage too.

fuel.sourcingBuildHere: Build here (pick a site on the map)
fuel.wtwHelp: Used for FuelEU Maritime compliance — replace with your Proof of Sustainability value.
fuel.consumptionHelp: Benchmark from the vessel type, or derived from distance when selected in the Vessel step.
fuel.prodOpex: Fuel production O&M, excl. fuel purchase
fuel.prodZeroNote: Forced to 0 under this sourcing — production cost lives inside the fuel price.
fuel.legacyPriceNote: Legacy Excel accounting: this merchant price is charged ON TOP of the production CAPEX/O&M below.

port.fossilNote: Fossil benchmarks assume existing infrastructure: CAPEX 0, OPEX at 30% of a new green facility.

regulation.phaseNote: Phase-in applied automatically: 40% in 2024, 70% in 2025, 100% from 2026.
regulation.targetNote: Target reduction applied automatically: 2% from 2025 stepping to 80% by 2050.
regulation.usProduced: Green fuel produced in the US
regulation.escalationHelp: 0 = flat nominal price — at 2% inflation that is a falling real price. Set equal to inflation to hold the real carbon price constant; the IMO framework’s remedial prices escalate by construction.
regulation.imoRewardHelp: The reward for zero/near-zero fuel surplus below the direct-compliance target. Genuinely undetermined at source — default 0; the surplus balance is reported in tonnes regardless.
regulation.imoNote: Draft MEPC 83 structure (approved Apr 2025; adoption targeted MEPC 85, Oct 2026 — provisional): attained WTW fuel intensity vs two reduction ladders against the 93.3 gCO2eq/MJ 2008 reference; deficits priced $100/t (tier 1, direct→base band) and $380/t (tier 2, beyond base). Ladders agreed 2028–2035 and held flat beyond; tier prices established 2028–2030.
regulation.imoNotParam: Not parameterised: the pinned reference bundle has no IMO Net-Zero rows — the module reports nothing rather than silently computing zero.

results.heading: Results
results.gapHelp: Green cost minus fossil cost — the gap a green premium or public support would need to close.
results.netReg: Net regulatory effect on the gap
results.bothBases: CO2 abated — combustion: {ttw} t · well-to-wake: {wtw} t
results.abatementNoteEts: The premium per tonne of CO2 avoided, next to the EU ETS allowance price you entered — the market’s going rate for a tonne.
results.abatementNoteSelf: The premium per tonne of CO2 avoided, next to your self-designed scheme’s carbon price — the rate this scenario actually charges.
results.abatementNoteImo: The premium per tonne of CO2 avoided, next to the IMO Net-Zero remedial price that applies in this scenario.
results.abatementNoteNone: No carbon price is active in this scenario — enable EU ETS, the self-designed scheme or the IMO framework to compare against one.
results.imoNotParam: IMO Net-Zero: not parameterised in the pinned reference bundle.
results.annualYear1Caption: Year 1 carries {capital} of green capital, charged in full up front — year 1 alone is {share}% of the lifetime gap.
results.intensityNote: The fossil fuel ({fossilWtw} gCO2e/MJ) exceeds {crossings} - from then on every tonne it burns is priced. The green fuel sits at {greenWtw} gCO2e/MJ for the whole horizon.
results.intensityNoteNoCross: Neither fuel ({fossilWtw} and {greenWtw} gCO2e/MJ) exceeds a compliance line within the horizon.
results.intensityDisabled: Neither scheme is enabled in this scenario - switch them on in the Regulation tab to price this.

buildHere.chip: cell {cell} · LCOH ${lcoh}/kg ({rate}%) · synthesis {nameplate} kt/yr, scale ×{scale} · {km} km to port
buildHere.configNote: Each component is a derived seed from the evaluation — edit any one to override just that line (the derived value stays as the restorable benchmark). Typical use: accept the map’s hydrogen cost, replace the synthesis plant with your EPC quote.
buildHere.pickOnMap: No evaluated site yet — click a coloured hex on the map, open the cell, choose “Use as corridor fuel site”, adjust any assumptions, press Calculate, then hand the result back.
buildHere.repickNote: Pick any other hex on the map to move the site.
buildHere.displayOnly: (display figure — the corridor discounts the raw CAPEX/OPEX)
buildHere.sizingLine: Plant sized to corridor demand: {demand} t/yr × {margin} margin = {nameplate} t/yr nameplate ({surplus} t/yr surplus — reported, never apportioned).
buildHere.rateWarning: The LCOH evaluation ran at {lcohRate}% while the corridor discounts at {corridorRate}%. The LCOH-internal rate is display-only — the corridor applies its own rate to these CAPEX/OPEX lines — but the site’s levelized $/kg was computed at the other rate.
buildHere.engineMoved: Evaluated with LCOH engine {evaluated}; current is {current}. Stored values still apply — re-run the evaluation on the map to refresh them (never automatic).
buildHere.sumLine: Production CAPEX = ${capex}m · production OPEX = ${opex}m/yr — the lines the corridor engine consumes.

scenarioBar.name: Scenario name
scenarioBar.resetConfirm: Start a new corridor? This clears the current draft.

corridor.legacyBanner: Legacy Excel accounting loaded: this scenario charges the merchant fuel price AND production CAPEX/O&M — production cost is counted twice. Preserved verbatim for workbook comparison; new scenarios cannot select this mode.
